I can't rule out down or around the edge to (3,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.

I can't rule out up, down or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going up would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.

Contradiction! Going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (up from number 3) was wrong. Next I'll try down.

I can't rule out around the edge to (5,6) or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (5,6).
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5); going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (6,5) would force the line onto number 14 before its turn. So the line goes down.
The line must go down: right is number 12, which comes later.
Going right would strand number 11: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going around the edge to (6,6) would wall in number 15, the last number. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
